title: User profile picture is displayed poorly when falling back to the software rendering
line: With software rendering, the user picture on the lock and login screens is round with its white border again instead of a square over the frame.
explanation: The lock and login screens' UserDelegate cuts the user picture round and draws its border with a ShaderEffect (UserDelegate.frag). Shader effects don't run with the software renderer, so there the plain square picture was shown over the translucent circle, with no border; the code even had a comment accepting that. The change adds a Canvas, used only with software rendering, that draws the picture clipped to the same circle (cropped like PreserveAspectCrop) and the same border; the GPU path is untouched.

commits.message:
lookandfeel: Draw the round user picture also with software rendering

The shader that cuts the user picture round and draws its border doesn't
run with software rendering, so the picture showed as a square over the
frame. Draw the same circle and border with a canvas in that case.

BUG: 408144

media.caption: Lock screen with software rendering, master: the square picture (white corner included) over the frame, no border
Same picture with the fix: cut round with the white border, as with GPU rendering
No user picture, software rendering, master: generic icon, no border
No user picture with the fix: the same border GPU rendering draws around the icon

review.text: Targeted, clean fix for a long-standing software-rendering visual defect in the lock and login screens' UserDelegate. Because ShaderEffect (and Kirigami ShadowedTexture / QtQuick Shapes image clipping) do not clip round under the Qt Quick software backend, falling back to a QML Canvas only when wrapper.softwareRendering is true properly matches the shader's circle crop and border while leaving the GPU path untouched. Before/after screenshots and verification of GPU parity, wide aspect ratios, no-avatar state, and resize animation are thorough.

reviews.text: Targeted, clean fix for a long-standing software-rendering visual defect in the lock and login screens' UserDelegate. Because ShaderEffect (and Kirigami ShadowedTexture / QtQuick Shapes image clipping) do not clip round under the Qt Quick software backend, falling back to a QML Canvas only when wrapper.softwareRendering is true properly matches the shader's circle crop and border while leaving the GPU path untouched. Before/after screenshots and verification of GPU parity, wide aspect ratios, no-avatar state, and resize animation are thorough.

This fixes exactly what the report and Nate's c7 describe: with software rendering the ShaderEffect is skipped, so the avatar was a square with no border. A Canvas used only in software mode clips the picture to a circle with the same radii as UserDelegate.frag (inner 0.47, border up to 0.49), crops it like PreserveAspectCrop and leaves the GPU path untouched. The screenshots prove both the picture and the no-picture case. A small nit: loadImage() keeps each user's full-size picture cached for the life of the greeter, with no unloadImage() when the source changes.
